title: Johnny Dunn, the Coarch trumpet and King Swayzee
summary: Phillips knew Johnny Dunn from records of Mamie Smith and the show Dixie to Broadway, explains the long Coarch trumpet, and recalls TOBA soloist King Swayzee.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What about Johnny Dunn? Did you ever listen to Johnny Dunn?
Yeah.
He was in the 20's.
Yeah, he was in the 20's.
Did you ever hear him live?
No, I never did hear him live.
You heard him on records?
Phillips - 147
Yeah, records. In them days, he had plenty of records -- the 20's. Because he was playing with Mamie Smith.
Right, and Perry Bradford...
Yeah. Then he got on this big show. They used to feature him on this show.
which show?
I forgot it. I think it was one of them shows like Runnin' Wild...
Dixie To Broadway?
Dixie To Broadway, that's what it was. He's the one that started playing that Coarch trumpet.
Is Coarch a brand name?

Yeah, it's one of them long ones. There's one in that picture of King. We had one in the band -- I had one. When you pick it up... It's like a trumpet that they blow in the Biblical days, but it was... They stood about that high.
About 4 feet high?

About 3 feet. It sounded like another trumpet, but it was just a novelty. Pappy(?) or Arthur Williams, he used to pick it up and blow a lot of solos on it. People said, 'Look at that. What is it he's blowing?' It was one of them things." Johnny Dunn, he used to take on Dixie To Broadway, he used to feature that on that show... They used to
Phillips - 148

feature him. So he'd just come out and play. In them days, a lot of cats used to just go around on those shows and they didn't nothin' but play solos themselves. There was another cat used to go around on the TOBA Time -- he was featured the same way. He played with Cab Calloway a while. He died. The man was from Little Rock, Arkansas. King Swayzee.
He's listed in Chilton's book. Did you know him back in Arkansas?

No. I knew him, I think, out on the road. He used to go travel on the TOBA Time, he and a cat named Sammy Lewis. Sammy sang and he played. Then later he went with Cab. In those days the trumpet players... Most of the other good trumpet players that were famous was in New Orleans. They hadn't left New Orleans.
Getting ready to go, but not yet.
Yeah. Johnny Dunn was out there by himself. Johnny was out there before Louis came.
